name: Multi agent competition

subjectOf.text: Multi agent competitive collaboration captures a diversity dividend worth more than half a standard deviation of quality improvement while enabling attribution through citation graphs.
subjectOf.abstract: Our multi-agent competitive collaboration protocol captures diversity dividends worth 0.5+ standard deviations of quality improvement while enabling attribution through citation graphs.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Evolution of Domain-Specific Reputation Systems From Binary Validation to Citation-Weighted Knowledge Attribution (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6192998
scope_conditions: quality approximately normally distributed across competing agents
competition size of roughly three to seven agents

subjectOf.text: The real barrier to multi agent competition is not cost but the absence of an attribution mechanism: if only the best of several competing agents is paid, the others have no incentive to participate, so competition requires rewards proportional to each contributor's contribution.
subjectOf.abstract: The real barrier is the lack of attribution mechanism. If 5 agents compete but only the best gets paid, the other 4 have no incentive to participate. We need a framework where all contributors can be rewarded proportional to their contribution.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Evolution of Domain-Specific Reputation Systems From Binary Validation to Citation-Weighted Knowledge Attribution (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6192998
scope_conditions: multiple agents competing on the same job

subjectOf.text: Multi agent competition improves attack resistance because it creates multiple attack surfaces that must all succeed simultaneously, and citation transparency makes collusion detectable; with a fifty percent quality penalty for detected collusion the corruption cost doubles relative to the original framework.
subjectOf.abstract: This improved security stems from multi-agent competition creating multiple attack surfaces that must all succeed simultaneously, combined with citation transparency enabling collusion detection.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Evolution of Domain-Specific Reputation Systems From Binary Validation to Citation-Weighted Knowledge Attribution (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6192998
scope_conditions: honest agents compete on quality in the same jobs

subjectOf.text: Domains using multi agent competition will exhibit fifteen to thirty percent higher quality scores than single agent selection, controlling for agent capability.
subjectOf.abstract: Expertise domains using multi-agent competition will exhibit 15-30% higher quality scores compared to single-agent selection, controlling for agent capability.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Evolution of Domain-Specific Reputation Systems From Binary Validation to Citation-Weighted Knowledge Attribution (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6192998
scope_conditions: parallel domains with identical expertise requirements
quality measured by blind expert review
